# 01 — Data analysis (generated by `scripts/analyze.py`)

Generated output. Do not edit by hand; rerun `python3 scripts/analyze.py`. All data is synthetic and must not be presented as real Mirantus figures. Source for every number in this file: [CSV].

- Export date: 2026-09-30
- Primary observation window: 457 days (15 months) after the first screening
- Small-cell threshold: cells with n<100 are marked directional

## 7. What the data cannot show

- The export has no column for the recommended re-screening interval. Columns present: customer_id, location_id, location_type, city, optician_follow_up, first_screening_date, age_band, preferred_language, result_category, report_opened, report_opened_days_after, marketing_consent, referral_booked, second_screening_date.
- Therefore "returned on time" cannot be measured per customer. The window rate above measures return within a fixed calendar window, not return relative to each customer's interval. A customer whose interval is longer than the window is counted as a non-returner in the window rate without being late.
- The longest follow-up in the export is 637 days (about 20.9 months). Any interval longer than that cannot be judged from this export at all; customers with such intervals are not judgeable, not non-returners.
- optician_follow_up is self-reported per location by the optician, not observed per customer; whether a given customer was actually contacted is unknown.
- Returns are only seen at mira locations; screenings or eye exams elsewhere are invisible.
- There is no data on reminders sent by Mirantus, on what the report says, or on why customers did not return.
